other_side: Zitron, in a paid piece of which only the opening is free to read, cites the same Bloomberg report that Big Tech shares rose on a bet that Democrats will slow AI spending. He reads it not as a soft landing but as the market treating the election as the end of the build-out. His argument is that Nvidia's growth depends entirely on unimpeded data centre construction, and that without more capacity OpenAI and Anthropic cannot sell stories based on infinite growth. Once that narrative takes hold, he says, "everything begins to implode".
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is whether capital spending can be trimmed without breaking what depends on it. Both accept as fact that Big Tech shares rose while chip makers and neoclouds fell, that the build-out was already behind schedule, and that less spending would improve hyperscaler cash flow. The empirical question is whether the hyperscalers can spend less while Nvidia, the neoclouds and the labs carry on; the observable is 2027 capital spending guidance in January's results, set against Nvidia's outlook and neocloud access to debt. The residue is worldview: whether demand is real enough that scarcity enriches compute owners, or whether growth itself was the product being sold. For Whittemore to be vindicated, spending must ease gently with no disorderly failures. For Zitron, lower spending must hit Nvidia's revenue and push leveraged builders into default. Both are polemicists with incentives: Whittemore bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype. The signal is that both now expect a slowdown. Watch the January capital spending guidance.
